summary: SSO tenant-binding mismatch blocks internal access request approvals
description:
Issue summary: After last night's org-alias rollout, internal access request approvals issued via the Support Console are not provisioning access. Approval workflows show 'Approved' in the UI but the approval webhook returns 403 from the auth service citing tenant binding mismatch in the incoming SAML/OIDC assertion.

Impact: Engineers cannot be granted temporary access to internal runbooks and oncall tools. This affects ~12 oncall handoffs in us-east since 02:00 UTC and is preventing escalation for high-priority incidents. No customer-facing functionality is affected, but internal incident response is degraded.

Environment: Production (us-east), all clusters for the approval-service and auth-proxy. Affected users span multiple teams; most are internal staff with active Okta sessions.

Initial detection: Support noticed multiple 'approved but not provisioned' reports and opened this ticket. Correlated with org-alias rollout (confluence page linked below).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Submit an access request for 'runbook-audit' via Support Console as a user with an Okta session.
2) Approve the request using the built-in approver flow (Support Console -> Approvals -> Approve).
3) Observe UI shows 'Approved' and approver activity log records success, but Provisioner logs show 403: tenant-binding mismatch and the user is not granted the role in RBAC store.
4) Reproduced with both web UI approval and API-triggered approval webhook (POST to /approvals/callback).
expected_behavior: Approved requests should trigger provisioning: approval webhook accepted by auth service, role granted in RBAC, and user receives access tokens/console role within the configured provisioning window.
actual_behavior: Approvals are reflected in the Support Console but provisioning fails with 403 from auth-proxy citing 'tenant binding mismatch' in assertion. The Auth microservice rejects assertion where 'tenant' claim in the session does not match expected tenant value derived from the approval payload.
logs: 2025-01-15T02:12:05Z auth-proxy debug: assertion parsed; tenant claim = org:prod:redwood-us; allowed-tenants = [org:prod:redwood, org:staging:redwood]
2025-01-15T02:13:10Z okta-logs (session) user: elena.c: saml_assertion tenant=org:prod:redwood-us; device=managed
investigation_notes: 00:30 - Support replicated locally: approval POST accepted but provisioning 403 from auth-proxy.
01:00 - SRE checked auth-proxy config: tenant mapping was recently updated by infra team to add alias 'redwood-us' during org-alias rollout (ref: CONFL-ORGS-2025).

01:40 - IAM confirmed that the approval payload uses canonical tenant 'org:prod:redwood' while Okta-supplied session assertions contain alias 'org:prod:redwood-us' for users in us-east due to attribute transform introduced in last rollout.

02:10 - Hypothesis: approval-service and provisioner expect canonical tenant, but auth-proxy strict-validate compares to allowed-tenants and rejects alias variants. The new alias was not added to auth-proxy allowed list.
02:45 - Temporary test: added 'org:prod:redwood-us' to auth-proxy allowed-tenants in staging; approvals provisioned successfully in staging replication.
03:20 - Root cause likely a configuration gap: org-alias rollout updated Okta attribute mappings but did not push equivalent alias mapping to auth-proxy/provider config used by provisioner.
03:50 - Risk assessment: If left unaddressed, all future alias rollouts will break provisioning across services that validate tenant claim strictly.
resolution: Mitigation applied: added 'org:prod:redwood-us' to auth-proxy allowed-tenants in prod at 2025-01-16T04:10 UTC. Provisioning resumed for affected approvals. Permanent fix: infra config PR to centralize tenant alias mapping and add a validation test in CI (PR: infra-config#872). Follow-up task created to audit other services that perform strict tenant validation.
comments: 2025-01-15T03:05Z - Eleanor Chen (Reporter): Noticed this while approving an oncall access request; created ticket. Users report they see 'Approved' but still can't access runbooks.
2025-01-15T03:25Z - Diego Alvarez (Assignee): Investigating auth-proxy logs and recent config changes. Hypothesis: tenant alias introduced in Okta mapping not known to auth-proxy.
2025-01-15T04:00Z - Priya Nair (IAM): Confirmed Okta attribute mapping added tenant alias 'redwood-us' last night (change ID CONFL-ORGS-2025). Approval payload still uses canonical 'redwood'.
